description: Voluntary frameworks and control catalogues for information security. Many are referenced by regulation or contractually required; all are voluntary at source.

issuing_bodies.name: US National Institute of Standards and Technology
issuing_bodies.remit: US federal standards agency. Guidance adopted globally.

issuing_bodies.name: Center for Internet Security
issuing_bodies.remit: Non-profit; publishes CIS Controls and CIS Benchmarks.

issuing_bodies.name: Cloud Security Alliance
issuing_bodies.remit: Cloud-specific security standards and certifications (CCM, STAR).

standards.name: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 — Information Security Management Systems
levels: Certification — audited by accredited certification body
standards.summary: International standard for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an Information Security Management System (ISMS). 2022 revision restructures Annex A controls.
key_principles: Context of the organisation — interested parties, ISMS scope
Leadership and commitment
Planning — risk assessment, risk treatment, objectives
Support — resources, competence, awareness, communication, documented information
Operation — operational planning, risk assessment and treatment implementation
Performance evaluation — monitoring, internal audit, management review
Improvement — nonconformity, corrective action, continual improvement
93 Annex A controls across 4 themes (organisational, people, physical, technological)

standards.name: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 — Information Security Controls
standards.summary: Reference set of information security controls providing guidance on selecting, implementing, and managing controls referenced in ISO 27001 Annex A.
key_principles: 93 controls across four themes: organisational (37), people (8), physical (14), technological (34)
Each control described with purpose, control, and guidance
Attributes for filtering: control type, information security properties (C/I/A), cybersecurity concepts, operational capabilities, security domains

standards.name: ISO/IEC 27017:2015 — Cloud services security controls
standards.summary: Cloud-specific extensions to ISO 27002, with additional cloud controls and implementation guidance for both providers and customers.
key_principles: Additional cloud-specific controls (e.g. shared responsibility, virtual machine security, administrator's operational security)
Guidance on applying existing 27002 controls in cloud contexts
Distinct guidance for provider vs customer

standards.name: ISO/IEC 27018:2019 — Protection of PII in public clouds
standards.summary: Guidance on PII protection for public cloud service providers acting as processors.
key_principles: Consent and choice
Purpose legitimacy and specification
Data minimisation
Use, retention, disclosure limitation
Accuracy and quality
Openness, transparency, notice
Individual participation and access
Accountability, information security, privacy compliance

standards.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
standards.summary: Voluntary framework structured around six functions: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover. 2.0 adds 'Govern' as an explicit function and expands beyond critical infrastructure.
key_principles: Govern — organisational cybersecurity governance
Identify — asset management, risk assessment, supply chain
Protect — access control, awareness, data security, platform security, resilient tech
Detect — continuous monitoring, adverse event analysis
Respond — incident management, analysis, response communication, mitigation
Recover — recovery plan execution and communication

standards.name: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 — Security and Privacy Controls
standards.summary: Catalog of security and privacy controls for federal information systems. Widely adopted by non-federal organisations. Referenced by FedRAMP, CMMC, and others.
key_principles: 20 control families covering access control, audit, awareness, configuration, incident response, etc.
Controls mapped to CSF functions and categories
Tailoring guidance for risk-based control selection
Privacy controls integrated with security

standards.name: NIST SP 800-63 — Digital Identity Guidelines
standards.summary: Guidelines for identity proofing, authentication, and federation. Four-volume series (base plus -A/-B/-C). Revision 4 expected 2025+.
key_principles: Separate assurance levels for identity proofing (IAL), authenticator (AAL), and federation (FAL)
Phishing-resistant multi-factor for high-assurance
Explicit handling of risk-based authentication
Privacy-preserving federation patterns
Memorised secrets (passwords) — relaxed composition rules, emphasise length and breach checks

standards.name: CIS Critical Security Controls v8
standards.summary: Prescriptive, prioritised set of cybersecurity actions. 18 controls with safeguards. Maps to NIST CSF, ISO 27001, and others.
key_principles: IG1 — basic cyber hygiene for small/medium organisations
IG2 — enterprise controls for those with dedicated security resources
IG3 — advanced controls for mature organisations
Community defense model — controls chosen based on attack pattern data

standards.name: CSA Cloud Controls Matrix v4
levels: Part of CSA STAR certification tiers 1-3
standards.summary: Cloud-specific control framework with mappings to ISO 27001/27017/27018, NIST, PCI-DSS, etc.
key_principles: 197 controls across 17 domains
Shared Responsibility Model guidance
Mappings enable reuse of existing compliance evidence
Basis for CSA STAR certification
